discovery: Theoretical prediction and establishment of altermagnetism as a third fundamental class of collinear magnetic order

nominees.name: Tomas Jungwirth
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Physics, Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague, Czech Republic

nominees.name: Libor Smejkal
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems, Dresden, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter physics: magnetism and spintronics
motivation: Using spin-group symmetry analysis, Smejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth showed that collinear magnets are not only ferromagnets or antiferromagnets. There is a third, symmetry-distinct phase, altermagnetism. In it, compensated sublattices related by rotations rather than translations produce zero net magnetization together with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting of d-, g- or i-wave character. This organizing principle was first set out in theory, including the earlier prediction of the crystal anomalous Hall effect. It was then confirmed experimentally by photoemission and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism imaging in MnTe, CrSb and related compounds. It brings together ferromagnetic-like spin-polarized transport and the robustness and terahertz dynamics of antiferromagnets. This opens new routes for spintronics, unconventional superconducting proximity effects and the study of intertwined orders. Jungwirth's earlier pioneering work on antiferromagnetic spintronics laid the foundation. It is a rare case of symmetry reasoning finding a new phase of matter in materials that were already known.
